name: Tavily Search
description: Tavily AI web search. POST a query and get ranked web results with relevance scores; optionally an LLM-synthesized answer, raw page content, and images. Supports topic (general/news/finance), date/time filtering, and domain include/exclude lists.

extra.name: USD Coin
extra.terms: By using the Tavily solution, you agree to be bound by the Terms of Use (https://tavily.com/terms) and Privacy Policy (https://tavily.com/privacy) and accept that Tavily disclaims any liability with regard to the AI agent and cryptocurrency payments.

usage.callShape: POST JSON {query (required, 1-1000 chars), max_results?, topic?, search_depth?, include_answer?, include_raw_content?, include_images?, time_range?, start_date?, end_date?, include_domains?[], exclude_domains?[]}. Only `query` is required.
usage.outputShape: results[].{url,title,content,score,raw_content}, answer, follow_up_questions, images[], query, response_time, request_id
quirks: Only `query` is required; all other fields optional.
answer is null by default — pass include_answer:true to get an AI-synthesized answer.
raw_content (per-result) is null by default — pass include_raw_content:true for full page text.
images[] is empty by default — pass include_images:true to populate.

On x402.tavily.com search_depth is fixed to 'advanced' (enum has only that value); the Orthogonal proxy exposes the full Tavily depth enum (advanced/basic/fast/ultra-fast) plus extra fields (chunks_per_source, country, auto_parameters, include_favicon, include_image_descriptions).
max_results accepts the string 'auto' or an integer 1-50.
x402.tavily.com uses x402 v2 (network eip155:8453); Orthogonal proxy uses x402 v1 (network 'base'). Same USDC asset, same $0.01.
content snippets are truncated with a [+N chars] marker in the default (non-raw) response.

usage.outputShape: {query, results[].{title, url, snippet, score, source ('brave'|'tavily'), confirmed_by? ('both' when the same URL surfaced from both providers)}, total, sources_queried[] (['brave','tavily']), deduplicated (count of dropped duplicate URLs)}
quirks: This is the fused/aggregator endpoint: it hits Brave AND Tavily in parallel and merges the results — distinct from the cheaper single-provider SignalFuse endpoints /v1/gateway/search/brave ($0.008, GET ?q=) and /v1/gateway/search/tavily ($0.012, POST).

Each result carries a `source` field; URLs seen from both providers are marked confirmed_by:'both'. `deduplicated` reports how many duplicate URLs were collapsed, so `total` can be smaller than brave_count + tavily_count.
max_results caps at 20 (default 10).
SignalFuse also offers free trial credits (POST /v1/credits/trial {wallet}, 5 credits) and a browser playground (signalfuse.co/play, 25 free calls/day) as alternatives to per-call x402 payment.
maxTimeoutSeconds is 300 in the 402 accepts (the fused call waits on two upstream providers).
usage.guide: Fused web search over Brave + Tavily. POST https://api.signalfuse.co/v1/gateway/search with x402 payment (~$0.015 USDC on Base, eip155:8453) and JSON body {query (required), max_results? (default 10, max 20)}. Returns merged, URL-deduplicated ranked results: {query, results[].{title,url,snippet,score,source,confirmed_by?}, total, sources_queried, deduplicated}. Use when you want breadth/cross-source confirmation in one call; use the cheaper single-provider SignalFuse Brave/Tavily endpoints when one source suffices.

name: 2s Research
description: Produce a grounded, cited research brief on any topic, entity, or question — gathers sources (Wikipedia plus any URLs you supply) and synthesizes a 2-4 sentence summary, key facts, and the source list, grounded only in the fetched sources (no free-form invention).

query.description: Topic, entity, or question to research.

urls.description: Optional source URLs to ground the brief in, alongside Wikipedia.

summary.description: 2-4 sentence factual summary grounded in the sources.

keyFacts.description: Bullet facts, each with an inline (Source N: <title>) citation.

usage.callShape: POST https://2s.io/api/ai/research with JSON body { query, urls? } — pay per call via x402 (USDC on Base or Solana). The brief is returned inline in the 200; no polling.
usage.outputShape: data.ok=true; data.items[0] = { query, summary (2-4 sentence factual synthesis), keyFacts[] (bullet facts each ending with an inline '(Source N: <title>)' citation), sources[]{title,url} }; data.total=1; data.source={provider:'2s.io AI (Anthropic Claude Haiku) + Wikipedia', url:'https://2s.io', license:'Generated content; Wikipedia content CC BY-SA.'}; plus top-level meta.cost.usd and meta.settlement{txHash,network,success}. Verified sample (query 'Ada Lovelace') returned a 4-sentence summary, 9 keyFacts, and 2 Wikipedia sources.
quirks: Input is a JSON body: 'query' (required, 2-400 chars) is the topic/entity/question; optional 'urls' (array, max 5, each <=2048 chars) supplies extra source pages to ground the brief in, alongside Wikipedia.

GROUNDED-ONLY: the brief is synthesized strictly from the fetched sources (Wikipedia + your URLs) with no free-form invention. Best for well-documented topics; obscure queries with no Wikipedia coverage and no supplied URLs will have little to ground on.
Upstream is 2s.io's own AI gateway: Anthropic Claude Haiku for synthesis over Wikipedia (per data.source). This is 2s.io's x402 endpoint, not a re-host of any single named model.

Billing is 'actual-usage-upto-max': the live 402 also offers an 'upto' scheme (Permit2 on Base, facilitatorAddress 0x2A89407a98A0732b7fD578c4E156B7166540EB5A) capped at the same $0.042; the two exact-scheme accepts (Base + Solana, first in accepts) charge the full amount. Observed exact-scheme charge was the full $0.042.
Free verification without paying: append ?trial=1 (or header X-2s-Trial:1) for one free real call per endpoint per hour — used here to pre-validate {query:'Ada Lovelace'} before the paid call.
Each keyFact string carries its own inline citation like '(Source 1: Ada Lovelace)' referencing the sources[] index/title.
usage.guide: Get a grounded, cited research brief on a topic. POST https://2s.io/api/ai/research with JSON body {"query":"<topic, entity, or question>"}, optionally adding "urls":[...] (up to 5) to ground the brief in specific pages alongside Wikipedia. Pay per call via x402 (USDC on Base or Solana, $0.042). Read the synthesis from data.items[0].summary, the bullet facts (with inline citations) from data.items[0].keyFacts[], and the source list from data.items[0].sources[]. The brief is grounded only in fetched sources (no invention), so prefer well-documented topics or supply your own URLs. Verified 2026-07-30 with {query:'Ada Lovelace'} -> HTTP 200, $0.042 charged.

name: 2s AI Search
description: AI web search optimized for agents: send a query and get ranked results, each with the extracted, LLM-ready page content (not just a link + blurb) and a relevance score. topic=news narrows to recent reporting.

usage.callShape: GET https://2s.io/api/search/ai?q={query}&maxResults={1-10}&topic={general|news} (x402 paid, no body)
usage.outputShape: Results are nested one level under body.data: body.data.ok (boolean), body.data.items[] each {title,url,content,score} where content is the extracted LLM-ready page text (truncated with a [+N chars] marker) and score is 0-1 relevance, body.data.total = count returned, body.data.source {provider,url,license}. Settlement/cost metadata under body.meta {endpoint,caller,cost.usd,settlement{txHash,network,success}}.
quirks: Results are wrapped under body.data (the endpoint's own envelope), not at the top level — read body.data.items[], not body.items[]
q, maxResults and topic are query-string params, not a JSON body; only q is required
content is truncated (each result ends with a [+N chars] marker) — it is a clean extract, not the full page
topic=news narrows to recent reporting; default is general web results
Distinct from 2s search.web (raw SERP) — this returns extracted page content per result, not just links + blurbs
Also accepts Solana USDC in addition to Base USDC; supports 2s trial (?trial=1) for one free real call per hour
usage.guide: AI web search built for agents. Send a GET to https://2s.io/api/search/ai with a required query param q (2-400 chars); optional maxResults (1-10) and topic (general or news). No request body. The x402 payment (~$0.018 USDC on Base, also Solana) is handled by the pay layer — no API key or signup. On success you get 200 JSON with results nested under body.data: iterate body.data.items[] and read each item's title, url, content (extracted, LLM-ready page text) and score (0-1 relevance); body.data.total is the count and body.data.source gives attribution. Use topic=news for recent reporting.

name: SocialFetch Web Search
description: Keyword web search over SocialFetch — returns ranked organic web results (title, URL, snippet) for a query, with optional country, recency, and pagination filters.

query.description: Search query text to run against the public web.

region.description: Optional ISO 3166-1 country code for localized results (e.g. US, GB, CA).

usage.callShape: GET https://api.socialfetch.dev/v1/web/search?query=<search+terms> — `query` is a required URL query-string param (1-500 chars); optional `region` (ISO country), `datePosted` (last-hour|last-day|last-week|last-month|last-year), `page` (1-based). No JSON body.
usage.outputShape: data.{query, results[].{title,url,content}}, meta.{requestId, creditsCharged, version, cached?}
quirks: Required query param is `query` (NOT `q`/`text`); it is validated up-front, so a bare request without it 400s before any 402/charge.
Auth is either an x-api-key header (bills SocialFetch credits) OR pay-per-request in USDC on Base via x402 v2 — we index the x402 path (no key). 1 credit = $0.014 per successful request.
Cached responses (meta.cached=true / Age header present) still charge the full endpoint price.
402 body says 'Missing API key' but the PAYMENT-REQUIRED header carries a valid x402 accepts and paid GET returns 200 — the label is misleading, the route is genuinely x402-payable.
usage.guide: Keyword web search over SocialFetch. GET https://api.socialfetch.dev/v1/web/search?query=<search+terms> — `query` required in the URL query string; optional region/datePosted/page filters; no body. Pay per call in USDC on Base via x402 ($0.014). Returns data.results[] of {title,url,content} ranked organic web results plus meta.{requestId,creditsCharged,version}.

name: 2s Web Search
description: Raw live web search (Brave-backed): send a query and get ranked results, each with title, URL, snippet description, site name and page age — fresh information past any model training cutoff. Supports paging, country, freshness and safesearch filters.

offset.description: Number of result pages to skip (pagination).

freshness.description: pd=past day, pw=past week, pm=past month, py=past year, or a YYYY-MM-DDtoYYYY-MM-DD range.

usage.callShape: GET https://2s.io/api/search/web?q={query}&count={1-20}&offset={0-9}&country={ISO2}&freshness={pd|pw|pm|py|range}&safesearch={off|moderate|strict} (x402 paid, no body)
usage.outputShape: Results nested one level under body.data: body.data.ok (boolean), body.data.items[] each {title,url,description(snippet),siteName,age(relative, e.g. '2 weeks ago', nullable),language}, body.data.total = null (Brave reports no count), body.data.source {provider:'Brave Search API',url,license}, body.data.meta {query,moreAvailable}. Settlement/cost metadata under body.meta {endpoint,caller,cost.usd,settlement{txHash,network,success}}.
quirks: Results are wrapped under body.data (the endpoint's own envelope), not at the top level — read body.data.items[], not body.items[]
q, count, offset, country, freshness, safesearch are query-string params, not a JSON body; only q is required

This is raw SERP (links + snippets, Brave-backed) — for extracted LLM-ready page content + relevance scores use 2s AI Search (/api/search/ai); for news-specific results with timestamps use /api/news/search
body.data.total is always null (upstream Brave does not report a count); use body.data.meta.moreAvailable + offset to page
offset caps at 9 (page offset, not result offset); count caps at 20
Also accepts Solana USDC in addition to Base USDC
usage.guide: Raw live web search built for agents (Brave-backed). Send a GET to https://2s.io/api/search/web with a required query param q (1-400 chars); optional count (1-20, default 10), offset (0-9 for paging), country (2-letter ISO), freshness (pd/pw/pm/py or a YYYY-MM-DDtoYYYY-MM-DD range) and safesearch (off/moderate/strict). No request body. The x402 payment (~$0.009 USDC on Base, also Solana) is handled by the pay layer — no API key or signup. On success you get 200 JSON with results nested under body.data: iterate body.data.items[] and read each item's title, url, description (snippet), siteName, age and language. body.data.total is null (Brave gives no count); use body.data.meta.moreAvailable with offset to page. For extracted page content instead of links, use 2s AI Search; for dated news use /api/news/search.

name: Agentstools Drug Label
description: Looks up a drug by name and returns the clinically important FDA structured-product-label (SPL) sections via openFDA — boxed warning, indications, dosing, contraindications, warnings, drug interactions and pregnancy — as compact cited text (informational, not medical advice).

drug.description: Drug brand, generic or active-ingredient name (required), e.g. 'ibuprofen'.
Echo of the requested drug name.

found.description: Whether a matching FDA label was found on openFDA.

identity.description: Resolved drug identity (brand/generic/manufacturer) when found; empty object when not found.

available_sections.description: Canonical label-section names present for this drug, e.g. boxed_warning, indications, dosage, contraindications, warnings, drug_interactions, pregnancy.

label_sections.description: Map of canonical section name -> { text, truncated (boolean — very long sections are truncated to a size cap), source_tag (the openFDA SPL field the section resolved from) }.

partial.description: True when some sections or the upstream lookup were incomplete.

errors.description: Per-provider error strings when an upstream lookup failed (e.g. openFDA rate-limit/403); response is still 200.

attribution.description: openFDA / U.S. FDA public-data attribution notice.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/drug/label?drug={drug name} (x402 paid, no request body). `drug` is the only param and is REQUIRED (brand, generic or active-ingredient name). Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous). Pays $0.015 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless. NOTE: the 402 quote is delivered in the `payment-required` response HEADER (base64 x402 envelope); the 402 body is an empty {}.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: query {drug} (echo), found (boolean), identity (object — resolved drug identity, empty when not found), available_sections[] (canonical section names present, e.g. boxed_warning/indications/dosage/contraindications/warnings/drug_interactions/pregnancy), label_sections{} (map of section name -> {text, truncated (boolean — long sections capped/flagged), source_tag (the openFDA SPL field it resolved from)}), sources {partial (boolean), providers[], errors{} (per-provider error strings on upstream failure — still 200)}, attribution[] (openFDA/FDA notice), disclaimer (not-medical-advice string). openapi documented example {drug:'ibuprofen'} shows found:true with available_sections [boxed_warning, indications, contraindications] and label_sections.contraindications {truncated:false, source_tag:'contraindications'}. At index time the live paid call for {drug:'ibuprofen'} returned 200 but found:false / empty label_sections because upstream api.fda.gov (openFDA) returned HTTP 403 (sources.errors.drug_label='upstream api.fda.gov returned HTTP 403', sources.partial:true) — the documented graceful-partial behavior.
quirks: The 402 quote is in the `payment-required` HEADER, not the body — the 402 body is a bare {} (2 bytes). A payer that only inspects the body will miss the accepts.

Flat price $0.015 USDC on Base only (amount 15000 atomic, USDC 6 decimals) — confirmed against both the live 402 header and the openapi x-payment-info fixed price; no Solana leg, not a dynamic ceiling.

Depends on the upstream openFDA (api.fda.gov) API, which can rate-limit/403 — the service degrades GRACEFULLY: it still returns HTTP 200 with found:false, empty label_sections, sources.partial:true and the failure recorded in sources.errors (never a 500). At index time openFDA returned 403, so the paid sample came back found:false; retrying later (or when openFDA is not throttled) should populate label_sections.

Section normalization is the moat: each canonical section (boxed_warning, indications, dosage, contraindications, warnings, drug_interactions, pregnancy) resolves through an ordered list of candidate openFDA SPL tags and takes the first present; the resolved tag is reported as label_sections[section].source_tag.
Very long sections are truncated to a size cap and flagged with label_sections[section].truncated:true to stay token-efficient.

Informational aggregation of public FDA data — NOT medical advice, NOT a diagnosis; the response carries a disclaimer and an openFDA attribution string that should be preserved when displaying results.
`drug` accepts brand, generic or active-ingredient names; partial/empty answers are returned cleanly rather than as errors.
usage.guide: Get the key FDA structured-product-label (SPL) sections for any drug with one keyless x402 call. Send a GET to https://api.agentstools.dev/drug/label with a single query param `drug` (REQUIRED — a brand, generic or active-ingredient name, e.g. 'ibuprofen', 'atorvastatin', 'Tylenol'); no request body. The x402 payment (~$0.015 USDC on Base) is handled by the pay layer — no API key or signup — but note the 402 quote comes in the `payment-required` header, and the 402 body is empty. On success you get 200 JSON: check `found`, then read `available_sections[]` for which canonical sections exist and iterate `label_sections{}` — each entry has `text` plus `truncated` (long sections are capped) and `source_tag` (which openFDA SPL field it came from). Canonical sections include boxed_warning, indications, dosage, contraindications, warnings, drug_interactions and pregnancy. This endpoint proxies openFDA (api.fda.gov), which can rate-limit: on upstream failure you still get a 200 with found:false, empty label_sections, sources.partial:true and the reason in sources.errors — treat that as 'try again later', not a crash. Always preserve the attribution[] and disclaimer (informational only, not medical advice). Example: {drug:'ibuprofen'} -> when openFDA is available, boxed_warning + indications + contraindications sections as cited text.

name: Agentstools Drug Profile
description: Clinical safety profile for a drug by brand/generic/active-ingredient name or NDC: fuses openFDA identity, approval status, key label sections, a FAERS adverse-event summary and a deterministic severity score into one cited JSON. Informational, not medical advice.

drug.description: Drug brand, generic or active-ingredient name, e.g. 'warfarin'. Provide either `drug` or `ndc`.

ndc.description: Product NDC instead of a name, e.g. '0093-1712'. Provide either `drug` or `ndc`.

label_openfda.description: openFDA identity block from the drug label, e.g. generic_name[], brand_name[], manufacturer_name[].

label_sections.description: Key structured-label sections (e.g. boxed_warning {truncated, source_tag}, contraindications, warnings).

total_reports.description: Total FAERS reports for the drug.

death_fraction.description: Fraction of reports with a death outcome.

errors.description: Per-provider upstream errors, keyed by provider id (e.g. drug_ndc, drug_drugsfda, drug_label, drug_event).

partial.description: True when one or more upstream openFDA sources failed and the profile is incomplete.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/drug/profile?drug={brand|generic|active-ingredient name} (or ?ndc={product NDC}) — x402 paid, no request body. Provide EITHER `drug` OR `ndc`. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous). Pays $0.04 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: query {drug, ndc}, identity {label_openfda {generic_name[], ...}, ndc_products[], approvals[]}, label_sections {boxed_warning {truncated, source_tag}, ...}, adverse_events {total_reports, death_fraction}, severity {score (0-100), band (low/high), flags {has_boxed_warning, has_contraindications, has_drug_interactions, significant_death_signal, significant_serious_signal}, reasons[], signals {boxed_points, serious_points, death_points, contraindication_points, interaction_points}}, sources {errors{}, partial (bool), providers[]}, attribution[] (openFDA notice), disclaimer (not-medical-advice). PROVIDER-DOCUMENTED fully-populated example for {drug:'warfarin'} (when openFDA is reachable): identity.label_openfda.generic_name=['WARFARIN SODIUM'], adverse_events {total_reports:133626, death_fraction:0.13}, severity {score:62, band:'high', flags.has_boxed_warning:true}, sources.partial=false. LIVE PAID CALL at index time returned 200 with the correct schema and the endpoint's own severity logic ran (score:0, band:'low', full flags/reasons/signals), but upstream api.fda.gov returned HTTP 403 for all four sub-providers (drug_ndc/drug_drugsfda/drug_label/drug_event) so identity/label_sections/adverse_events were empty and sources.partial=true — a transient openFDA throttle, not an endpoint defect.
quirks: Provide EITHER `drug` (name) OR `ndc` (product NDC, e.g. '0093-1712') as a query param; the response echoes both under `query` with the unused one null.

This is a FAN-OUT over openFDA (api.fda.gov): NDC directory + Drugs@FDA approvals + structured labeling + FAERS adverse events. When openFDA rate-limits or 403s (it throttles unauthenticated bursty callers), the corresponding sections come back empty and sources.partial=true with per-provider errors under sources.errors — retry later for a complete profile. Observed at index time: all four sub-providers returned 'upstream api.fda.gov returned HTTP 403'.

The `severity` block is computed deterministically by this endpoint from whatever openFDA data was retrieved; when data is missing it can read score:0/band:'low' with reason 'no boxed warning or notable adverse-event signal found in public data' — treat a low score as low-CONFIDENCE, not low-risk, whenever sources.partial=true.
label_sections values may be truncated (fields carry truncated:true + source_tag); fetch the raw label via the sibling /drug/label endpoint for full section text.
402 advertises Base USDC only ($0.04, amount 40000, 6 decimals); no Solana leg on this endpoint.

Informational aggregation of public FDA data only — NOT medical advice, NOT a diagnosis; preserve the attribution[] and disclaimer strings when displaying results (openFDA data does not imply FDA endorsement).
usage.guide: Get a one-shot clinical safety profile for any drug with a single keyless x402 call. Send a GET to https://api.agentstools.dev/drug/profile with EITHER ?drug={name} (brand, generic or active-ingredient, e.g. 'warfarin', 'ibuprofen', 'lisinopril') OR ?ndc={product NDC, e.g. '0093-1712'} — no request body. The x402 payment (~$0.04 USDC on Base) is handled by the pay layer — no API key or signup. On success you get 200 JSON fusing openFDA sources: identity (label_openfda generic/brand names, ndc_products, Drugs@FDA approvals), label_sections (boxed_warning and other key sections, may be truncated), adverse_events (total_reports and death_fraction from FAERS), and a deterministic severity block (score 0-100, band low/high, boolean flags for boxed warning / contraindications / drug interactions / death & serious signals, plus reasons[] and a signals[] point breakdown). ALWAYS check sources.partial: if true, one or more openFDA sub-providers (drug_ndc/drug_drugsfda/drug_label/drug_event) failed — see sources.errors — and the profile (and its severity score) is incomplete, so retry later before trusting a low score. Preserve attribution[] and disclaimer. Informational only, not medical advice. Example: {drug:'warfarin'} -> when openFDA is up: generic_name WARFARIN SODIUM, 133626 FAERS reports, death_fraction 0.13, severity 62/high with a boxed warning.

name: Agentstools Nutrition Search
description: Keyword food search over USDA FoodData Central (public domain): returns ranked food matches with fdc_id, description, brand, GTIN/UPC, serving size, food category and key macros per 100g (calories, protein, fat, carbohydrates).

total_hits.description: Total number of matching foods in USDA FoodData Central.

count.description: Number of matches returned in this response.

data_type.description: USDA data type (Branded, Foundation, SR Legacy, Survey (FNDDS), Experimental).

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/nutrition/search?q={food name}&limit={1-25}&dataType={Foundation|SR Legacy|Branded|Survey (FNDDS)|Experimental} (x402 paid, no request body). `q` is REQUIRED; `limit` (default 10) and `dataType` are optional. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous). Pays $0.002 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: query (echo of q), total_hits (integer — total matching foods in USDA FDC), count (integer — matches returned), matches[] each {fdc_id (USDA FDC id), description, data_type (Branded/Foundation/SR Legacy/Survey (FNDDS)/Experimental), brand (nullable), gtin_upc (nullable), serving_size {amount, unit, household}, food_category, macros_per_100g {calories_kcal, protein_g, fat_g, carbohydrates_g}}, attribution (USDA public-domain notice). Live verified for {q:'cheddar cheese', limit:5}: total_hits 60790, 5 branded cheddar records e.g. fdc_id 2057648 GRAFTON VILLAGE, macros_per_100g {calories_kcal:393, protein_g:21.4, fat_g:28.6, carbohydrates_g:3.57}.
quirks: `q` (food name) is the only required param; `limit` defaults to 10 and is capped at 25; `dataType` optionally filters to a single USDA data type.
macros are always normalized PER 100 GRAMS (macros_per_100g), independent of the food's own serving_size — convert to a serving using serving_size.amount if you need per-serving values.

data_type distinguishes record provenance: 'Branded' (commercial products with brand/GTIN) vs 'Foundation'/'SR Legacy'/'Survey (FNDDS)' (generic USDA reference foods, no brand); use dataType=Foundation/'SR Legacy' for generic ingredient macros.
total_hits can be very large (e.g. 60790 for 'cheddar cheese') — this is the full USDA corpus count; only `limit` records are returned, so refine `q` for precision.
brand and gtin_upc are null for non-Branded records.
402 advertises Base USDC only ($0.002); no Solana leg on this endpoint.
Data is from USDA FoodData Central (public domain); the response includes an attribution string that should be preserved when displaying results.
usage.guide: Search the USDA FoodData Central food database and get key macros for any food with one keyless x402 call. Send a GET to https://api.agentstools.dev/nutrition/search with query params (no request body): q (REQUIRED — the food name, e.g. 'cheddar cheese', 'raw broccoli', 'chicken breast'), optional limit (1-25, default 10) and optional dataType (one of Foundation, 'SR Legacy', Branded, 'Survey (FNDDS)', Experimental) to filter to generic vs branded records. The x402 payment (~$0.002 USDC on Base) is handled by the pay layer — no API key or signup. On success you get 200 JSON: read total_hits (full corpus match count), count, and iterate matches[] — each has fdc_id (USDA FoodData Central id), description, data_type, brand (null unless Branded), gtin_upc, serving_size {amount, unit, household}, food_category, and macros_per_100g {calories_kcal, protein_g, fat_g, carbohydrates_g}. Macros are always per 100 g; scale by serving_size.amount for per-serving values. Use dataType=Foundation or 'SR Legacy' for generic ingredient nutrition, or Branded for a specific packaged product. Preserve the attribution string (USDA public domain). Example: {q:'cheddar cheese', limit:5} -> 5 branded cheddar records, macros_per_100g ~393 kcal / 21g protein / 29g fat.

name: Agentstools Web Search
description: Free-text web search that returns a ranked, URL-deduped list of title/url/snippet results from a multi-engine fusion (Brave, DuckDuckGo, Google, Wikipedia, Yandex and more) in one call, with optional freshness, locale, safesearch and engine-pin filters.

backend.description: auto (default multi-engine fusion) or a specific engine: brave/duckduckgo/google/mojeek/startpage/wikipedia/yahoo/yandex, or a CSV of them.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/search?query={text}&max_results={1-20}&timelimit={d|w|m|y}&region={us-en|uk-en|de-de|...}&safesearch={on|moderate|off}&backend={auto|brave|duckduckgo|google|mojeek|startpage|wikipedia|yahoo|yandex|CSV} (x402 paid, no body; only query is required)
usage.outputShape: Top-level JSON: query (echo), count (integer), results[] each {title, url, snippet}. Live verified: 5 real current web results for 'x402 protocol' (Wikipedia X2, plus RBC/Habr/Gate/GitHub pages) with title, url and a ~1500-char snippet each.
quirks: Only query is required; all other params optional. Omitting max_results returns the provider default result count

Despite the summary saying 'DuckDuckGo', the default backend is a multi-engine auto-fusion (Brave, DuckDuckGo, Google, Wikipedia, Yandex, Mojeek, Startpage, Yahoo) deduped by URL and re-ranked; pin backend= to force a single engine or a CSV of engines
max_results is capped at 20
region defaults to us-en and safesearch defaults to moderate
results are locale/engine-dependent — a query can surface non-English pages (e.g. RBC/Habr Russian results here); set region to bias locale

usage.guide: Resolve any clinical trial to a clean, normalized profile with one keyless x402 call. Send a GET to https://api.agentstools.dev/trials/study with a single query param `nct` (REQUIRED — a ClinicalTrials.gov NCT id such as 'NCT03228186'; `id` is an accepted alias); no request body. The x402 payment (~$0.02 USDC on Base) is handled by the pay layer — no API key or signup — but note the 402 quote comes in the `payment-required` header and the 402 body is empty. On success you get 200 JSON: check `found`, then read `trial` for identity (nct_id, brief_title, org), status (overall_status, why_stopped, key dates, results_posted), design (study_type, phases, enrollment), sponsor (lead, lead_class, collaborators), conditions[], interventions[{type,name}], primary_outcomes[], locations[] + location_count, and a computed signals block (is_recruiting, is_active, has_results, days_since_update, days_to_primary_completion, enrollment_type). An unknown id returns found:false rather than an error. Always preserve attribution[] and disclaimer — this is public ClinicalTrials.gov (NIH/NLM) data, informational only, not medical advice. Example: {nct:'NCT03228186'} -> a terminated Phase 2 NSCLC trial (Pevonedistat + Docetaxel, University of Michigan Rogel Cancer Center, 40 enrolled, results posted).
